label: input q at late original positions (t >= 5)
explanation: Fires when the input token is the letter q during the original (pre-<DEL>) phase at position t >= 5. Never fires at t <= 4, on the delimiter, or anywhere in the copy phase (including q fed back as input there); essentially never on any other token (34 tiny activations on other tokens at t=8, ~0% mass). Magnitude grows with position: t=5 is weak (only ~70% of q at t=5 are active, ~4% of mass) while t=6..8 fire on every q and carry ~96% of mass; top activations (~2.8) are q at t=8 just before <DEL>. Not modulated by surrounding tokens, first token, or repetition. False positives are all weak/inactive q at t=5.

issues: No refutation found. Every claim I tested held up. On the test split the predicate scores P 0.884, R 0.999, F1 0.938, mass recall 1.0, which matches the reported numbers.
Phase claim: the profile shows 0 activations on the delimiter and 0 in the copy phase. The predicate (phase != 0) & q covers 90,774 steps (test) and has precision 0.
Position claim: there are 0 activations at t <= 4. On dev, q at t >= 6 gives precision 1.0 (16,500 of 16,500 active) and 96.3% of the mass. q at t == 5 gives precision 0.70 and only 3.7% of the mass.
Mean activation per active step rises from t=5 to t=8 (mass share divided by count goes 5 < 6 < 7 < 8), so 'magnitude grows with position' holds.

All false positives are q at t=5. I looked for a systematic cause of t=5 inactivity and found none. Precision barely moves with L (L=6 0.69, L>=7 0.71), in_first (0.71 vs 0.67), a digit before (0.79, n=1479), a vowel before (0.74), n_digits, or seen(DIGITS) (0.72 vs 0.69). This looks like t=5 activations sitting near the firing threshold, not a hidden condition.
Missed activations: 30 on test, all at step 8 on non-q tokens, all at <= 0.04 of max, holding 0.0% of the mass. This is scattered noise.
Small caveat: by count, t=5 holds about 32% of activations even though it holds only about 4% of the mass. The explanation's 'weak at t=5' covers this.
